gaps.note: The founders step into the hallway to privately discuss the multi-shark deal.
The founders return to the tank after their hallway discussion.

stage_a.note: The presenting team communicates a strong, positive, and engaging demeanor throughout the pitch.
The founders show sustained engagement and excitement when demonstrating the product and listing their awards.
The team presents in a friendly, approachable manner, sharing personal anecdotes warmly.

venture.description: Wearable reading glasses that wrap around the wrist and snap open when needed.
venture.note: The product is reading glasses that function as a wrist accessory.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark introduces himself to the panel.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Kenzo introduces himself, states the ask, and opens with a question about unrelated food items.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark explains they were bought by mistake because he forgot his reading glasses.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Kenzo describes the frustration people have when they need reading glasses but do not have them.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark demonstrates how the reading glasses wrap around the wrist and snap open to be worn.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Kenzo asks his father to show the mechanism one more time.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark demonstrates the glasses snapping open and closed again.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Kenzo explains that the patented design allows the glasses to spring open and snap shut.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Kenzo mentions the product has received four international design awards.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark adds that the reading glasses are fashionable.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark asks which investor is interested in forming a strategic partnership.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Kenzo invites the panel to try the samples provided in front of them.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark Cuban praises the presentation as the best pitch ever.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara asks if the wristbands come in different sizes to fit various wrists.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Kenzo explains they are starting with a universal one-size-fits-all model that covers the vast majority of the population.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara asks if they hold a utility patent on the design.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark confirms they have utility patents in the US, China, and Japan, with European countries pending.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks if the grippers on the band leave a mark on the skin after extended wear.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark explains he wears them constantly and while they may leave a slight mark, it is not bothersome.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark Cuban notes that the glasses are intended for on-the-go use rather than long-term reading.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara agrees with Mark Cuban that they are meant for on-the-go use.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Kenzo confirms they are designed for the many brief moments a day when someone quickly needs to read something.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark Cuban asks for the manufacturing cost and the retail selling price.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Kenzo states that they cost thirty dollars and fifty cents landed and sell for one hundred ten dollars online.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond asks Mark if he is an inventor by trade.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark explains it was born of a personal need when he kept forgetting his reading glasses.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara asks Kenzo if he has a background in engineering.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Kenzo confirms he holds a bachelor's and a master's degree in structural engineering from Cornell University.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara asks Kenzo how he developed the idea for the mechanism.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Kenzo explains he applied the physics principles used in skyscrapers to the small scale of the glasses.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara jokingly asks Mark for his reaction to being outwitted by his son.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark jokes that starting a business is tough but doing it with a child is even harder.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara asks Mark to share his own background since they had not heard it yet.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark shares he left home early, worked as a woodworker, and eventually founded several companies including Gorilla Glue.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara expresses extreme surprise at Mark being the founder of Gorilla Glue.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark confirms and jokes with the panel about the famous glue brand.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond asks Mark if he sold the company, noting its massive current scale.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark confirms that he sold the company years ago.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks Mark if the sale resulted in a good financial outcome for him.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark explains that every company he has sold included a royalty component, which worked out very well.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks Mark to verify that he mentioned a royalty.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark confirms that he did indeed say royalty.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks for details regarding their sales figures and how many units they have sold.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Kenzo details their recent website launch, twenty-eight thousand dollars in sales, and their profitable ad spend testing.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara asks Mark how much of his own money he has invested in the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark reveals he has put about six hundred thirty thousand dollars into the company.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond asks Mark why he needs a shark if he already has substantial funds.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark explains that his time is passed to build another company, and he wants to leave his son in good hands.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara expresses strong endearment toward Mark after his heartfelt explanation.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin states his clear intention to make the founders an offer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori becomes visibly emotional and apologizes while crying.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori explains that Mark's desire to secure his son's future deeply touched her, and expresses her strong interest.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori offers twenty-five thousand dollars for a ten percent stake, citing her expertise in the business.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin offers fifty thousand dollars for a ten percent stake, praising the product's social media potential.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark Cuban asks the founders what their decision-making criteria are for choosing a partner.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Kenzo explains they need the know-how to successfully distribute the product.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara asks Mark directly whether he would prefer Lori or Kevin as a mentor for his son.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark deflects choosing one, stating they are open to all of the above or multiple partners.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark Cuban notes the founders have flexibility because it is a great deal with retail, online, and licensing components.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark agrees that licensing the technology is a major opportunity for the business.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond offers to join Lori's deal, doubling whatever she has if she allows him in.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori states she would be happy to work with Daymond on the deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark tells Lori that ten percent equity is too high, despite the invaluable expertise the sharks bring.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks Mark to clarify if he is unwilling to give up that much equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark briefly confirms that Kevin's understanding is correct.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks if Mark would be willing to give up ten percent if he got three sharks.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark briefly agrees to the idea of three sharks for ten percent.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin proposes they do the deal with him included in the syndicate.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark Cuban declares he would love to be in the deal too.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara states she does not want to be left out of the deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks Mark what equity he would give up to have all five sharks.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark throws the question back to the panel, asking what terms would work for all five.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark Cuban suggests the founders step into the hall so the sharks can discuss a joint offer.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Kenzo agrees and asks for a second to step out.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: In the hallway, Kenzo tells his father he does not want to give up more than fifteen percent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mark tells Kenzo to let the sharks work it out.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: In the tank, Mark Cuban proposes a twenty-five percent total equity split among the five sharks.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Barbara points out the founder never said he would entertain twenty-five percent.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark Cuban replies that they are going to find out if he will accept it.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark Cuban welcomes them back, noting it is unprecedented that all five sharks want to back them.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori offers them one hundred twenty-five thousand dollars for twenty-five percent for all five sharks.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Kenzo counters the five-shark offer, proposing twenty percent equity instead.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori accepts the founders' counter-offer on behalf of the panel.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Kenzo enthusiastically accepts the revised five-shark deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin and the other sharks congratulate the founders on closing the deal.

decisions.note: Lori offers to invest because she knows the business and can put her heart behind it.
Kevin makes a competing offer because he is impressed with them.
Daymond offers to join Lori's deal, doubling the investment amount.
Kevin proposes a syndicate of three sharks for ten percent total equity.
Lori offers a deal including all five sharks for twenty-five percent equity.
Kenzo counters the five-shark offer, asking to give up twenty percent instead.
Lori accepts the founders' counter on behalf of the panel.
Kenzo enthusiastically accepts the revised five-shark deal.

record.notes: The founders step into the hallway during the negotiation to discuss the terms privately, which is included as part of the encounter.
